result.summary:
06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity.R is written (752 lines, md5 851bdf0c67ce21bb0eb61b488d0124f9) and runs cleanly in test mode. With the final version, a run from a deleted test folder followed by a second run from a fresh R process gave 28 of 28 byte-identical CSVs. The full run was not started, as instructed.

What the script does: a registry of 16 analyses (A0 to A5; all in legacy mode, A0, A1 with the F test and A2 also in corrected mode, so 22 fits), each one methylKit::calculateDiffMeth call on a methylBase object built directly from united_cpg_<mode>.csv.gz and reshaped with reorganize(). It writes analyses.csv, dml_counts.csv, dml_<analysis id>_<mode>.csv, interaction_vs_shared_<mode>.csv, dispersion_summary.csv, the figure, and per-fit caches. Beyond the specification it also writes equivalence_with_step05.csv and session_info.txt.

A0 is fitted first and checked against step 05 before anything else is fitted. On the 20,000-CpG test sample its p-values agree with step 05 to 5.1e-15 (relative) and its differences to 5.3e-14 points, in both modes. The full-run branch of that check (q-values, both DML lists, loci in both lists) could not be run on the real data, so I exercised the unmodified script in full mode on a stand-in project of 20,000 CpGs per mode whose "step 05 outputs" were regenerated with step 05's own code path: it passed, and nine kinds of tampering with the stand-in inputs each stopped the run.

Sources: I read the methylKit 1.28.0 code and documentation and the full text of Akalin et al. 2012. Wreczycka et al. 2017 I could check only in the preprint version, through a fetch tool that returns short quotes; the journal page returned 403. The header states what each source says and no more. The wording of I-06 in issues.md is stronger than the source and I propose an adjustment.

Heads-up from the test sample (not results, not in the proposed issues text): the median dispersion at eligible CpGs is about 3.6; with the MN correction and the F test none of the primary DML in the sample passed (0 of 45 ploidy, 0 of 91 heat; 2 and 5 with the chi-squared test); the uncorrected interaction test called 754 loci against 45 and 91 for the main effects. The full run will probably show that very few DML survive the correction.

Full run command, with WGBS_SENSITIVITY_SUBSET unset: WGBS_CACHE_DIR=/home/user/gannet_cache WGBS_CORES=2 Rscript 06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity.R
design_decisions: Reference lists come from step 05 files, not from this script. dml_ploidy, dml_heat and dml_shared of the same mode (with the class column) are read and restricted to the tested CpGs. In a full run A0 must reproduce p-values, q-values, both lists (loci and directions) and the loci in both lists (loci and classes), otherwise the script stops. In test mode only p-values and differences are checked, because SLIM q-values depend on the set of CpGs. Reason: the task names dml_shared_<mode>.csv and its class column as the reference, and this makes A0 a real check instead of a self-comparison.

A0 is fitted and checked before any other analysis, so a full run that cannot reproduce step 05 stops after two fits instead of after all of them. Reason: my choice, to save hours on a failed full run.

A0 is called with explicit overdispersion = "none", test = "Chisq" instead of bare defaults. In methylKit 1.28.0 logReg the line test = ifelse(test == "F" & phi > 1, "F", "Chisq") turns the default F into the chi-squared test whenever no dispersion is estimated. I confirmed identical() output of the default and the explicit call on 3,000 CpGs. The registry rejects test "F" with overdispersion "none" so that it cannot describe a test that is not run.

Effect sizes of the ploidy and heat contrasts are methylKit's own meth.diff, not recomputed. My pooled percentages are used only as a cross-check (asserted to agree within 1e-6 points in every main-effect analysis) and for the interaction. Reason: one CpG (NW_022994958.1:20934; heat 128 of 256 reads, control 182 of 260) has a difference of exactly 20 points, stored as -19.999999999999996. A different order of floating-point operations could put it on the other side of the cutoff and break the equivalence with step 05.

Interaction effect size is (triploid heat minus triploid control) minus (diploid heat minus diploid control), from pooled coverage-weighted group percentages, as the task specifies. The interaction DML files carry the four group percentages as extra columns after the six standard ones. "hyper" means a positive contrast; analyses.csv and the header define it.

The interaction coding is verified at run time. For each uncorrected A2 fit the script compares methylKit's p-values with the likelihood ratio test of ploidy:heat in a GLM written as ploidy * heat, at 200 seeded eligible CpGs, and stops above a relative difference of 1e-6. The registry also requires covariates "ploidy + heat" and all four groups for the interaction contrast. Reason: the claim that the indicator test is the interaction test is the basis of A2, so it is checked instead of asserted.

Outputs beyond the specification: equivalence_with_step05.csv (the A0 check with numbers), session_info.txt, and in test mode TEST_RUN_NOT_RESULTS.txt. Extra columns: n_significant (q below the cutoff without the effect-size criterion), n_in_primary_same_direction, primary_list, figure_label in analyses.csv, share_above_1 in dispersion_summary.csv, and run_scope in every summary table.

Keeping test and full outputs apart: every file is written through one function, out_file(); test mode redirects it to test_subset/. The summary CSVs carry a run_scope column, the figure a bold subtitle, and the folder a marker file. Section comments refer to "the output folder of this run" and never to a literal path. This is how I read the instruction that the header of every CSV-producing section must not confuse the two.

Cache signature: each RDS stores the analysis settings, the library ids, the indicator vector, the covariate values, the md5 of the united file, the CpG set (all, or subset size and seed), the number of CpGs and the methylKit version. A cached fit is used only when the signature is identical; otherwise the script says so and refits. Reason: a resumed run must not silently reuse a fit made from other input.

Warnings: the per-CpG warnings of glm.fit and methylKit (fitted probabilities of 0 or 1, no convergence, full model equal to reduced model, NaN replaced by 1) are counted and logged per fit. Any other warning stops the run. With more than one core these warnings are raised in forked workers and do not reach the parent, and the log says so.

Registry validation stops on: malformed or duplicated id, unknown contrast, library set, covariate, overdispersion or test; a mode not in config$modes; fewer than two libraries in a group; a design that is not of full rank; no residual degrees of freedom; an interaction without both main effects; and any change that would make A0_ploidy or A0_heat differ from step 05.

One seed (20261119, the seed of go_random_cpg_control.R) is set immediately before each random draw (test subset, dispersion sample, coding-check sample). Results therefore do not depend on whether fits are cached or on the number of cores.

Dispersion is computed with glm.fit(family = quasibinomial) as the Pearson statistic over the residual degrees of freedom from the final fitted values. This is exactly the quantity methylKit's MN option estimates in A1 before it sets values below 1 to 1. When fewer than 5,000 CpGs are eligible, all are used and the log says so. The sample size (5,000), the marks (1, 1.5, 3), the coding-check size (200), the tolerance (1e-6) and the smallest accepted subset (1,000) are settings at the top of the script, because run_config.R was not to be edited.

Citations in the header say only what I checked. Akalin et al. 2012 is cited for the test and SLIM, with the statement that it does not mention overdispersion and takes summed read coverage as the sample size. Wreczycka et al. 2017 is cited for its benchmark findings with the note that it was read in the preprint version (doi:10.1101/109512). McCullagh and Nelder 1989 is cited only as the source that methylKit's documentation names. The help page of stats::anova.glm is cited for the F test. The header does not declare one test the recommended one: both are run and the authors choose.

Figure: one panel per contrast with its own x scale (patchwork), one column per mode, horizontal stacked bars. The part of a list that is also in the primary list takes the DML-set colour of config$colours$dml_set; the rest is grey55. I ran the three colour pairs through the dataviz skill's palette validator on a white surface: colour-vision-deficiency separation at least 13.1, normal-vision separation at least 19.9, grey contrast 3.4 to 1. Counts are labelled at the bar ends and a thin line marks the size of the reference list. A row without a number was not run in that mode.

Figure labels are generated from the registry fields (family, library set, overdispersion and test), not typed per analysis, so a new registry entry needs no label and a label cannot disagree with its definition.

A header note on reading list sizes was added on my own judgement: analyses on fewer libraries and the interaction contrast pass the difference cutoff by chance more often, so without the correction they can return more DML than the primary analysis. Reason: without it the uncorrected A2, A4 and A5 counts invite the wrong reading.

The global holding the run-scope text is named scope_text and the column run_scope, so that no variable shares a name with a column inside a data.table call (the hazard named in the task). I checked every data.table call for such clashes by hand and with codetools.

Full-run outputs under 06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity/ are not git-ignored (only cache/ and test_subset/ are). They are small CSVs and a figure, and the project rule is that files that can live on GitHub should.
validation: A0 equivalence on the test subset (WGBS_SENSITIVITY_SUBSET=20000, seed 20261119), final script: largest relative difference in p-values against diffmeth_<contrast>_<mode>.csv.gz was 5.12e-15 (legacy ploidy), 5.07e-15 (legacy heat), 5.09e-15 (corrected ploidy), 4.97e-15 (corrected heat). Largest absolute difference in meth.diff was 5.33e-14 points. Both are the rounding of the 15-digit CSV. Although q-values are computed on the sample, the A0 lists contained every primary DML in the sample: legacy 45 of 45 ploidy and 91 of 91 heat; corrected 51 of 51 and 118 of 118.

Full-run code path, exercised without a full fit: a scratch harness built a stand-in project (copy of run_config.R, 02_R_functions, the library sheet and the script) whose step 05 tables are a different random sample of 20,000 CpGs per mode, regenerated with step 05's own code path (make_methylraw, methylRawList, unite, calculateDiffMeth with defaults, the list rules of write_mode). The unmodified script run there in full mode gave: p-values within 5.11e-15, q-values within 5.02e-15, differences within 5.33e-14; DML lists identical (legacy 48 ploidy and 97 heat, corrected 55 and 107); loci in both lists identical including classes (10 and 13); exit 0. No fit exceeded 20,000 CpGs.

Failure injection in the stand-in project, each ending with exit 1 and a specific message: one step 05 p-value multiplied by 1.01 (stopped before any A1 fit); one q-value multiplied by 0.9; a row dropped from a DML list; a row added; one direction flipped; one class of the shared list changed; a step 05 file deleted; two libraries swapped in the header of the united table. Swapping the counts of two libraries with the header intact invalidated the cache, forced a refit, and then stopped (largest relative p difference 9.3e12, effect difference 22 points). This shows the check catches a wrong library order. After restoring the inputs the run passed again.

What the methylKit options compute, on 3,000 random CpGs against my own computation from stats::glm: largest relative difference in p was 5.8e-9 for overdispersion none, 5.8e-9 for MN with F, 5.8e-9 for MN with Chisq. meth.diff was identical across the three options. The default call and the explicit none/Chisq call returned identical() data frames.

Interaction coding: methylKit's p-value for the indicator with ploidy and heat as covariates against the likelihood ratio test of ploidy:heat was within 1.9e-8 (relative) over 3,000 random CpGs in scratch, and within 5.8e-13 (legacy) and 1.6e-13 (corrected) at the 200 eligible CpGs checked at run time. The MN with F version agreed with my own computation within 1.9e-8. methylKit's meth.diff for this coding equals triploid heat minus all other libraries (within 2.0e-14) and correlates 0.66 with the interaction contrast, so it is not the interaction.

reorganize() and covariates: after dropping the four acute heat shock libraries the object keeps sheet order (checked by column content), and p-values equal my own GLM on the 18 libraries within 3.5e-8. The control-only fit without covariate equals my own GLM exactly (difference 0). In every main-effect analysis of every run the pooled group difference computed by the script agreed with methylKit's meth.diff (asserted at 1e-6; observed at most 5.3e-14).

Dispersion estimator: against summary(glm(family = quasibinomial))$dispersion on 300 eligible CpGs the largest relative difference was 7.9e-5 (summary.glm uses working weights from one iteration earlier). The sampling branch for more than 5,000 eligible CpGs was exercised on the first 150,000 rows of the legacy table (18,524 eligible, 5,000 sampled); a repeat gave an identical table.

Determinism, final script: a run from a deleted test folder (exit 0, 11.6 minutes on a loaded machine) followed by a second run from a fresh R process (exit 0, 0.3 minutes, 22 cached fits) gave 28 of 28 byte-identical CSVs. Across script versions, two independent from-scratch runs gave byte-identical files for all 27 CSVs whose content the edits in between did not touch; analyses.csv changed only through wording edits. One fit refitted with WGBS_CORES=1 gave the same CSVs as with 2 cores.

Cache handling: two cache files with altered signatures (a changed md5; a changed indicator string) were detected and refitted with the log line "the cached fit was made from other input or settings; fitting again"; all other fits were reported as cached. A dummy file dml_A9_removed_legacy.csv in the output folder produced the stale-file note and did not change any output.

Warning tally with one core: A0_heat in corrected mode logged 2 x "Full model does not deviate from Reduced model." and 4952 x "glm.fit: fitted probabilities numerically 0 or 1 occurred"; A4_ploidy_in_control logged none. A unit test of the counter with an mclapply-style message ("scheduled core 2 did not deliver a result") raised an error.

Input validation: WGBS_SENSITIVITY_SUBSET set to abc, 10, 20000.5, -5, 99999999999 and 5000000 each stopped with a message. Nine registry mistakes (interaction without both covariates, F without MN, duplicated id, unknown library set, aliased covariate, interaction within one ploidy, unknown mode, altered A0, malformed id) each stopped with a message naming the row and the reason.

Borderline CpG: NW_022994958.1:20934 has a heat-minus-control difference of exactly 20 points (stored -19.999999999999996, q 0.000385 in legacy mode). Recomputed from the CSV counts through the script's construction it gets the same value, is not above the cutoff, and is absent from the step 05 list, as here. Over 301 neighbouring rows the membership rule agreed with step 05 for every row.

Static checks: the file parses; codetools::checkUsage on its 18 functions reports only data.table column names and script-level globals; no non-ASCII character, no em dash, no occurrence of "desiccation"; no line longer than 170 characters; no setwd and no absolute path.

Resources in test mode: the R process stayed at about 1.0 to 1.2 GB resident memory. A from-scratch test run took 9.8 to 12.7 minutes of wall time on the shared machine; the 22 fits summed to 9.6 minutes in the quietest run.

Figure: rendered and inspected in test mode (bold TEST RUN subtitle) and in the stand-in full mode (no subtitle). I fixed colliding axis labels between the two mode panels, the offset of the count labels, the weight of the reference line, and the caption.
caveats: The full analysis was not run. Everything specific to full scale is an estimate or was tested only on a 20,000-CpG stand-in: run time, memory (I expect under 3 GB for the parent process with 2 cores), and the A0 list identity on the real data. The borderline-CpG check and the stand-in run make me expect A0 to reproduce step 05 exactly, but that is confirmed only when the full run logs "A0 reproduces the q-values, both DML lists and the loci in both lists of step 05" for both modes.

Run time: estimated_full_run_minutes (225) is for WGBS_CORES=2, from scaling the timed 20,000-CpG fits linearly to 480,579 and 454,555 CpGs (legacy about 157 minutes, corrected about 68). With 4 cores I expect roughly 2 hours. The machine was shared during timing, so treat this as plus or minus 30 percent. Serial parts of methylKit (uniquecombs, SLIM, reorganize) may not scale linearly.

Indicative only, from the test sample: median dispersion about 3.6 at eligible CpGs (94 percent above 1.5, 63 percent above 3); with MN and F no primary DML in the sample passed; uncorrected within-cohort and interaction lists were several times longer than the primary lists and nearly empty with the correction. These are not results and are not in the proposed issues text. If the full run confirms them, I-06 becomes decisive for every DML-based result, and the authors should be prepared for that.

Scratch exploration, not part of the script: recomputing q-values within eligible CpGs only (from cached p-values, no extra fits) did not change the corrected lists in the sample (0 and 0 DML for MN with F; 2 and 5 for MN with Chisq). The near-empty corrected lists are therefore not an artefact of testing many CpGs that cannot be DML.

Wreczycka et al. 2017: the journal page (ScienceDirect) returned 403. I checked the preprint version of 2017-08-09 (bioRxiv, doi:10.1101/109512), posted one week before online publication, through the WebFetch tool, which returns short quotations chosen by a small model. I did not read the journal PDF. The quotations used are in the proposed I-06 text; someone with journal access should confirm them against the published version.

The existing I-06 text says the benchmark shows a "markedly higher false positive rate" and "recommends" MN with the chi-squared test. The source words I could check are weaker and two-sided: lowest specificity, but also best overall accuracy for the uncorrected test; the corrected chi-squared test is "a good compromise", and the corrected F test is grouped with the stringent methods. I propose aligning I-06 with these words.

Akalin et al. 2012 was checked in the Europe PMC full text (PMC3491415) by keyword search and reading the passages on the test, covariates, SLIM and thresholds. The word overdispersion does not occur in it.

Not tabulated: the intersection of the two within-cohort ploidy lists (the replication table that I-01 mentions). It was not among the requested outputs; the two lists are written, so it is a small addition to a later step.
Not run: the heat shock as a covariate (third option of I-04). The registry supports the covariates ploidy and heat only.

The script stops if config$modes does not contain every mode named in the registry (both legacy and corrected). This is deliberate, so that a mistyped mode is not skipped silently, but a user who restricts config$modes must edit the registry.
Per-CpG warnings are not collected when WGBS_CORES is above 1 (they are raised in forked workers). Run one analysis with WGBS_CORES=1 to see the counts.

The counts tested are the normalized counts of step 05, scaled by 1.00 to 1.31 per library (library_filtering_legacy.csv). The binomial model treats them as real read counts, so a small part of the measured dispersion comes from that scaling. This is far too little to explain a median near 3.6, but it is a further reason why the uncorrected test is anticonservative for the control libraries.

In test mode I used WGBS_SENSITIVITY_SUBSET=20000 for every run of the script in the repository. The only other fits were scratch checks on 3,000 CpGs, the stand-in project (20,000 CpGs per mode, run in full mode without the variable), and invalid values of the variable that stop before any fit.

Repository state: I ran no git command that changes state. The parent session's snapshot commits picked up earlier versions of the script while I worked; the final version is in the working tree as a modification of the last snapshot. The working tree also shows a modified 01_pipeline/12_qpcr.R, which is not my change.

Two shell commands were refused by the permission system during the literature check: a curl download of the preprint PDF with a browser user-agent string, and a read of the proxy README. I did not pursue either and used the WebFetch tool instead.
The folder 06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity/ currently holds only test_subset/ (git-ignored). The README and issues texts are proposals; I edited neither file.
result.readme_text:
**Row to add to the table under "Files" in `06_diagnostics/README.md`:**

| `dml_sensitivity.R` | Sensitivity of the DML calls of step 05. The per-CpG tests are repeated under each alternative that the audit raises, and each resulting DML list is compared with the list of the draft. One methylKit fit per analysis and mode (22 fits): about 4 hours with `WGBS_CORES=2`, about 2 hours with 4 cores (estimated from timed fits on a sample of CpGs). Fits are cached, so an interrupted run resumes. | Folder `dml_sensitivity/` (tables, DML lists, figure; see "Sensitivity of the DML calls") |

**Lines to add to the run block:**

```sh
Rscript 06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity.R                                 # full run, after step 05
WGBS_SENSITIVITY_SUBSET=20000 Rscript 06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity.R   # test of the code on a random sample of CpGs, about 10 minutes
```

**New section:**

## Sensitivity of the DML calls

`dml_sensitivity.R` shows how the DML lists of step 05 change under each defensible alternative to the analysis of the draft, so that the authors can decide what the paper should report. Each analysis is one entry of a registry in the script and one `methylKit::calculateDiffMeth` call on the CpGs of `united_cpg_<mode>.csv.gz`. All analyses therefore test the same CpGs, and a DML is defined as in step 05 (`config$dml_qvalue`, `config$dml_difference`).

| Analysis | What it changes | Issues |
|---|---|---|
| A0 | Nothing: ploidy with heat as covariate and heat with ploidy as covariate, as in step 05. It is fitted first, and the script stops unless it reproduces the p-values, q-values, both DML lists, and the loci in both lists of step 05 | |
| A1 | Overdispersion correction (`overdispersion = "MN"`), once with the F test and once with the chi-squared test | I-06 |
| A2 | A tested ploidy by heat interaction, without and with the correction, set against the loci in both primary lists. Because heat is confounded with cohort, it is a ploidy by cohort interaction | I-02, I-01 |
| A3 | Both contrasts without the heat libraries that also had the acute heat shock | I-04 |
| A4 | Ploidy among the controls alone and among the heat-treated libraries alone, without and with the correction | I-07, I-01 |
| A5 | Heat against control among diploids alone and among triploids alone. Still a contrast between cohorts | I-01 |

All analyses run in `legacy` mode. A0, A1 with the F test, and A2 also run in `corrected` mode (I-05).

Files in `dml_sensitivity/`:

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `analyses.csv` | The registry: question, tested indicator, libraries, group sizes, covariates, overdispersion, test, residual degrees of freedom, definition of the effect size |
| `equivalence_with_step05.csv` | A0 against step 05: largest differences in p-values, q-values, and effect sizes, and whether the lists are identical |
| `dml_counts.csv` | One row per analysis and mode: CpGs tested, CpGs with q below the cutoff, DML, hyper, hypo, and the overlap with the primary list of the same contrast (`n_primary`, `n_in_primary`, `share_of_primary_recovered`, `share_of_list_in_primary`) |
| `dml_<analysis id>_<mode>.csv` | The CpGs that pass: position, p-value, q-value, effect size, direction. The interaction lists also hold the four group percentages |
| `interaction_vs_shared_<mode>.csv` | The loci in both primary lists, by class, and all other CpGs: how many have a significant tested interaction, with and without the effect-size criterion |
| `dispersion_summary.csv` | Dispersion of the read counts (Pearson chi-squared over residual degrees of freedom, model ploidy + heat) at 5,000 random eligible CpGs: quartiles and the shares above 1, 1.5, and 3. The model of the draft assumes 1 |
| `figure_dml_sensitivity.png`, `.pdf` | DML per analysis for each contrast and mode, with the part that is also in the primary list |
| `session_info.txt` | R and package versions of the run |

How to read the list sizes. The difference between two small groups is noisier than the difference between two large ones and passes the 20-point cutoff by chance more often. The analyses on fewer libraries (A3, A4, A5) and the interaction (A2, four groups of five or six libraries) can therefore return more DML than the primary analysis when no overdispersion correction is applied. A longer list is then not by itself evidence of more differences. Compare each uncorrected analysis with its corrected counterpart (`_mn_f`) and with `dispersion_summary.csv`.

Test mode. `WGBS_SENSITIVITY_SUBSET=<N>` runs the same code on a seeded random sample of N CpGs of each united table and writes everything to `dml_sensitivity/test_subset/`. That folder and the `cache/` folders are git-ignored. The files of a test run test the code and are not results: q-values depend on the set of CpGs tested.

## Result of the sensitivity analyses

To be written after the full run.
result.issues_text:
**Line for the "Updates" list at the top of `issues.md`:**

- 2026-11-19: `06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity.R` written and tested on a random sample of CpGs. I-01, I-02, I-04, I-05, I-06, and I-07 now say which of its outputs inform them and how to read them. Numbers follow the full run.

**I-01, paragraph to append:**

**Update 2026-11-19 (script written; full run pending).** The within-cohort analyses are analyses A4 and A5 of `06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity.R`; outputs are in `06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity/`. A4 tests diploid against triploid among the 12 control libraries alone and among the 10 heat-treated libraries alone, on the CpGs of step 05. Both are free of the cohort confound. Read `dml_counts.csv`, rows `A4_ploidy_in_control` and `A4_ploidy_in_heat`: `n_dml` is the size of the within-cohort list, `n_in_primary` the number of its loci that the draft also reports, and `share_of_primary_recovered` the share of the draft's ploidy DML that one cohort alone supports. The rows ending in `_mn_f` apply the correction of I-06. The loci are in `dml_A4_*_legacy.csv`. A ploidy difference that replicates is one that is in both A4 lists with the same direction; the script writes the two lists and does not tabulate their intersection. A5 tests heat against control within each ploidy. It is still a contrast between cohorts and does not address this issue; it shows only whether the heat list depends on the ploidy used. The tested interaction of I-02 is a ploidy by cohort interaction for the same reason.

**I-02, paragraphs to append:**

**Update 2026-11-19 (script written; full run pending).** Option 2 is analysis A2 of `06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity.R`. The indicator "triploid and heat-treated" is tested with ploidy and heat as covariates. With both main effects in the null model this is the likelihood ratio test of the ploidy by heat term; the script confirms it against a model written as ploidy * heat. methylKit's `meth.diff` is not the interaction for this coding, so the effect size is computed as (triploid heat minus triploid control) minus (diploid heat minus diploid control), from pooled percent methylation. An interaction DML has a q-value below the cutoff and an absolute contrast above the difference cutoff of step 05.

How to read `interaction_vs_shared_<mode>.csv`. Each row is a group of CpGs: the loci in both primary lists by class, all of them, every other tested CpG, and all tested CpGs. `n_interaction_significant` counts the CpGs with an interaction q-value below the cutoff, and `n_interaction_dml` those that also pass the effect-size cutoff. The row "in both primary lists, all classes" says how many of the draft's "interaction-DML" show an interaction when it is tested. The row "not in both primary lists" says how many tested interactions the overlap misses. `A2_interaction` uses the model of the draft; `A2_interaction_mn_f` adds the correction of I-06. The loci, with the four group percentages, are in `dml_A2_*_<mode>.csv`. The uncorrected count must be read together with `dispersion_summary.csv`: the interaction contrast compares four groups of five or six animals, so it is noisier than a main effect, and a test that treats reads as independent calls such differences significant. Whatever the counts, the text must call this a ploidy by cohort interaction (I-01).

**I-04, paragraph to append:**

**Update 2026-11-19 (script written; full run pending).** The sensitivity is analysis A3 of `06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity.R`: both contrasts of step 05 without the four libraries, on the same CpGs. Read `dml_counts.csv`, rows `A3_ploidy_no_acute` and `A3_heat_no_acute`: `share_of_primary_recovered` is the share of the draft's DML that are still called without the four libraries, and `share_of_list_in_primary` is the share of the reduced list that the draft also reports. A change is not a measure of the effect of the heat shock. The reduced analysis has three heat-treated animals per ploidy instead of five, and that alone changes which loci pass (see the note on list sizes in `06_diagnostics/README.md`). The option of a heat-shock covariate is not among the analyses.

**I-05, paragraph to append:**

**Update 2026-11-19 (script written; full run pending).** A0, A1 with the F test, and A2 of `06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity.R` run in both modes, so the effect of the overdispersion correction (I-06) and the tested interaction (I-02) can each be read with and without the coverage filter: column `mode` of `dml_counts.csv`, and `interaction_vs_shared_corrected.csv`.

**I-06, paragraphs to append:**

**Update 2026-11-19 (script written; full run pending).**

*Sources, as checked.* Akalin et al. 2012 (Genome Biology 13:R87, doi:10.1186/gb-2012-13-10-r87; full text searched and the passages on the test read) does not mention overdispersion. It states that "the relevant sample sizes in logistic regression are not merely the number of biological samples but rather the total read coverages summed over all samples in each group", which is the assumption at issue. In the benchmark of Wreczycka et al. 2017 the default test "showed the lowest specificity" and "has the best accuracy overall but highest false positive rate"; the F test with the correction "has similar results to DSS", one of the stringent methods; and "a good compromise between stringent and relaxed methods seems to be Chi-squared test with overdispersion correction". Their simulation had three samples per group. These quotations are from the preprint version of August 2017 (bioRxiv, doi:10.1101/109512); the journal page could not be opened from the audit environment, so they should be confirmed against the published version. The sentence above ("markedly higher false positive rate", "recommends") is stronger than these words and should be aligned with them. The R documentation of `stats::anova.glm` states that the F test is the most appropriate one when the dispersion is estimated by moments.

*What the option does* (methylKit 1.28.0, function `logReg`, confirmed against `stats::glm`). `overdispersion = "MN"` estimates a dispersion per CpG as the Pearson chi-squared statistic of the full model over its residual degrees of freedom, sets estimates below 1 to 1, and divides the deviance difference by it. The result is referred to a chi-squared distribution with 1 degree of freedom (`test = "Chisq"`) or to an F distribution with 1 and the residual degrees of freedom (`test = "F"`, applied only where the estimate is above 1). The differences in percent methylation do not change.

*How to read the outputs of `06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity.R`.* `dispersion_summary.csv` gives the distribution of that dispersion estimate at 5,000 random eligible CpGs under the model ploidy + heat. The model of the draft assumes 1. A value of 3 means that the counts vary three times as much as that model allows, so that its test statistics are about three times too large. `dml_counts.csv`, rows `A1_*`, gives the DML lists with the correction, by test; `share_of_primary_recovered` is the share of the draft's DML that remain. Rows `A2_interaction_mn_f` and `A4_*_mn_f` apply the same correction to the interaction and to the within-cohort contrasts.

**I-07, paragraph to append:**

**Update 2026-11-19 (script written; full run pending).** The control-only analysis is `A4_ploidy_in_control` of `06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity.R`: diploid against triploid among the 12 control libraries, on the CpGs of step 05 so that the list can be compared with the reported one. The list is `dml_A4_ploidy_in_control_legacy.csv`. `dml_counts.csv` gives the comparison: `n_in_primary` (loci in both lists), `n_in_primary_same_direction`, `share_of_primary_recovered` (the share of the reported ploidy DML that are also DML among the controls alone), and `share_of_list_in_primary` (the share of the control-only DML that the draft reports). If the text keeps "under control conditions", this is the list it describes.

**How to read each table (general note, for whichever issue or README section holds it):**

- `analyses.csv`: one row per analysis. `tested_indicator` and `group_sizes` say what is compared and with how many libraries; `residual_df` is the denominator of the F test; `effect_size_definition` says what a positive effect size means; `primary_list` names the step 05 list that the analysis is compared with.
- `equivalence_with_step05.csv`: must show TRUE in every check column of a full run. It is the evidence that analysis A0 of the script is the analysis of step 05, so that every other row differs from the draft by exactly one stated change.
- `dml_counts.csv`: `n_significant` is the number of CpGs with q below the cutoff before the difference criterion; `n_dml` applies both criteria; `n_primary` is the size of the step 05 list; `n_in_primary` is the overlap; the two shares express the overlap relative to the primary list and relative to the new list.
- `dml_<analysis id>_<mode>.csv`: the loci, for any follow-up (regions, genes).
- `interaction_vs_shared_<mode>.csv` and `dispersion_summary.csv`: see I-02 and I-06.

findings.summary: dml_counts.csv reports list sizes only. A short corrected list cannot be read as 'no signal' or as 'no power', and nothing shows that in the draft's analysis the q-value criterion removes no CpG. The header (lines 93-104, 131-139) and the proposed README and issues text warn only against over-reading long uncorrected lists.
findings.failure_scenario: The full run that is in progress already holds A0 and A1 (MN, F) for legacy mode: ploidy 1,038 DML against 2, heat 2,351 against 16. With the present columns (n_significant, n_dml, overlap) both corrected rows read 'almost nothing survives', and the authors cannot tell which of two opposite readings holds for which contrast. For ploidy the corrected p-values at eligible CpGs are close to uniform and random relabelling of the animals gives as many loci as the true labels, so 'the corrected test is merely too strict, keep the 1,038' would be wrong. For heat the corrected p-values are far from uniform although only 16 CpGs pass, so 'there are no differences between the cohorts' would be wrong too: a first discovery at q < 0.01 among 480,579 tests needs an F statistic above 84 with 19 residual df, 251 with 10 (A4 controls) and 474 with 8 (A4 heat).
findings.evidence: Reviewer's computations; scripts and outputs in the scratch directory named in the notes. (1) Step 05 tables: every CpG with an absolute pooled difference above 20 points has q < 0.01 for ploidy (1,038 of 1,038 legacy; 952 of 952 corrected) and all but one for heat (2,351 of 2,352 legacy; 2,273 of 2,273 corrected). The draft's lists are therefore an effect-size filter; the test removes one CpG in four lists (q_criterion_binding.R). (2) Caches of the full run, legacy, 65,480 eligible CpGs, share of p-values below 0.05 / 0.01 / 0.001: A0_ploidy 33.4 / 21.1 / 11.7 percent; A1_ploidy_mn_f 5.7 / 1.2 / 0.14 percent (uniform: 5 / 1 / 0.1); A0_heat 42.6 / 30.0 / 19.1 percent; A1_heat_mn_f 11.0 / 3.6 / 0.67 percent (full_pdist.R). (3) Ploidy labels permuted among the libraries of each cohort, 500 permutations on the full legacy table, pooled percentages only, no model fit: median 736 CpGs above 20 points (5th to 95th percentile 521 to 1,570, maximum 3,170) against 1,038 with the true labels; 12.8 percent of permutations give at least 1,038 (second seed: 12.6 percent; corrected mode: 952 observed, median 698, 14.6 percent) (permutation_effect_size_full.R). On the 20,000-CpG sample, six permuted labellings run through calculateDiffMeth with the draft's settings gave 20, 22, 23, 29, 31 and 49 DML against 45 for the true labels, and in each of them every CpG above the difference cutoff had q < 0.01 (permutation_null_subset.R). (4) qf(0.01/480579, 1, df, lower.tail = FALSE) is 84, 90, 251 and 474 for df 19, 18, 10 and 8; the chi-squared value for the same p is 31 (power_note.R). (5) SLIM is not the cause: its estimate of the share of true nulls is 0.80 to 0.95 in all 22 fits of the sample, and lists made with Benjamini-Hochberg q-values differ by at most 4 CpGs (pi0_by_analysis.R).
findings.suggested_fix: No refit is needed: the cached fits hold all p-values and the signature does not depend on the script text. Add to each row of dml_counts.csv: n_effect_above_cutoff (CpGs with an absolute effect size above config$dml_difference, whatever q) and the share of eligible CpGs with p below 0.05, 0.01 and 0.001 (`eligible` already exists in run_mode). Add a ploidy reference that needs no model fit: permute the ploidy labels among the libraries of each cohort (set.seed(seed), for example 1,000 permutations), count the CpGs whose pooled difference exceeds the cutoff, and write the distribution next to the observed count (about one second per ten permutations on the full table). Add to the header, the README section and the I-06 text: the F statistic a first discovery needs at each residual df; that a short corrected list is not by itself evidence of absence; that the q-value criterion is not binding in the draft's analysis; and that a test that shares information across CpGs (DSS, already named in I-02) or a region-level test is the route to calls with adequate power. The permutation numbers above come from the reviewer's scratch code and should be reproduced by the pipeline before they are quoted.

findings.summary: A cache file that was cut short stops the resumed run instead of being refitted, and the error does not name the file.
findings.failure_scenario: The process is killed (out of memory on the shared machine, or by hand) while saveRDS() at line 446 writes fit_<analysis id>_<mode>.rds. Writing one full fit takes about 0.4 s of an 8 minute fit, so the chance per interruption is small but not zero over 22 fits. The next run reads the partial file at line 425 and stops with a bare R error. The header (lines 41-42) promises that an interrupted run resumes where it stopped; the user has to work out from the log which file to delete.
findings.evidence: Scratch mirror, test mode: fit_A5_heat_in_triploid_legacy.rds cut to half its size. The run used the cached fits up to A5_heat_in_diploid and then ended with exit 1: 'Error in readRDS(cache_file) : error reading from connection / Calls: lapply ... analyse -> fit_analysis -> readRDS' (exp_truncated_cache.log). The other cache guards work: a file with an altered united_md5, and a full-run cache file (480,579 rows) copied into the test cache folder, were both reported as 'made from other input or settings; fitting again', refitted, and the 28 CSVs were byte-identical afterwards (exp_stale_signature.log, exp_full_cache_in_test_folder.log).
findings.suggested_fix: Write to a temporary name in the same folder and file.rename() it into place. Read with cached <- tryCatch(readRDS(cache_file), error = function(e) NULL) and treat NULL like a signature mismatch, with a log line that names the file.

findings.summary: A set but empty WGBS_SENSITIVITY_SUBSET selects the full run.
findings.failure_scenario: A wrapper or a shell line such as WGBS_SENSITIVITY_SUBSET=$N Rscript 06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity.R with N undefined exports the variable empty. Sys.getenv(unset = "") cannot tell empty from unset, so test_mode is FALSE and the script starts the full analysis (22 fits on all CpGs, hours on 2 to 4 cores) and writes into the folder of the full run, although the caller asked for a test.
findings.evidence: The first expressions of the script, evaluated in a scratch mirror with the variable set to '': 'test_mode = FALSE; subset_n = NA; out_dir ends with 06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity; scope: all tested CpGs'. The values ' 20000', '20000 ' and '2e4' stop with the intended message; '020000' is accepted as 20000 (exp_envvar.R).
findings.suggested_fix: subset_request <- Sys.getenv("WGBS_SENSITIVITY_SUBSET", unset = NA_character_); test_mode <- !is.na(subset_request). The existing pattern check at line 178 then rejects an empty value.

findings.summary: When the full-run check of A0 against step 05 fails, the message does not say which check failed, and equivalence_with_step05.csv is not written, so the folder keeps the table of the last successful run.
findings.failure_scenario: config$dml_difference or config$dml_qvalue is changed in run_config.R (or methylKit is upgraded) and the diagnostics script is run before step 05 is rerun. A0 is read from the cache, the lists differ, and the run stops at line 622 with 'A0 does not reproduce the q-values or the DML lists of step 05'. The log line above it reports p-values and differences equal to about 5e-15, so the user cannot tell whether the q-values, one list, or the shared loci differ, or by how much, and the message points to a numerical problem when the cause is a settings mismatch. The table that documents the check is written only at line 691, after all modes; the old file with TRUE in every column stays in the output folder next to the new analyses.csv.
findings.evidence: Code, lines 611-625 and 687-691: both stop() calls precede write_table(equivalence, ...), and neither prints the row of `equivalence`. Not exercised by the reviewer, because the list checks run only without WGBS_SENSITIVITY_SUBSET. findings.summary: The reference value of 1 for the dispersion is not what binomial reads give for the counts the script analyses.
findings.failure_scenario: dispersion_summary.csv, the comment at line 481, header lines 33-35 and the proposed README and I-06 text ('The model of the draft assumes 1') present 1 as the value under the binomial model. The counts are the normalized counts of step 05, each library multiplied by 1.00 to 1.31 and rounded. Purely binomial reads give about 1.2 after that scaling, so share_above_1 is high without any variation among animals and share_above_1_5 has a baseline near 20 percent. A reader who checks the two lower marks against 1 overstates the departure; a referee who knows this can dismiss the table.
findings.evidence: Simulation with the real scaling factors (library_filtering_legacy.csv, mean 1.16) and real coverages, 5,000 CpGs, binomial reads, the script's estimator: raw counts mean 1.01, median 0.98, 48 percent above 1, 7 percent above 1.5; after step 05's scaling and rounding mean 1.20, median 1.17, 68 percent above 1, 20 percent above 1.5 (sim_normalization_baseline.R). The observed dispersion is far beyond this baseline (reviewer's computation for the full legacy table: median 3.67, 94 percent above 1.5, 63 percent above 3), so the conclusion of I-06 stands.
findings.suggested_fix: State the baseline in the header, the README section and the I-06 text. Better, add to dispersion_summary.csv a seeded reference row: the same estimator on binomial counts simulated with the coverages of the sampled CpGs and passed through scale_counts_like_methylkit() with the factors of library_filtering_<mode>.csv.

independent_checks: Library order (check 1): for 6 random CpGs per mode, each of the 22 raw coverage files was searched and scaled with that library's factor; 132 of 132 (library, CpG) triplets per mode equal columns coverage<j>, numCs<j>, numTs<j> of united_cpg_<mode>.csv.gz for row j of the library sheet. This also rules out a swap of two libraries of one group, which the A0 check cannot see and which would make A3 drop the wrong library (check_library_order.R).

methylBase construction and reorganize (checks 1 and 2): the script's own make_methylbase() and fit_analysis() were run on 496 CpGs with methylKit::calculateDiffMeth intercepted, so that the object and arguments of every registry row were captured. getData() of the object is identical() to the input table; index slots are 5,8,...,68 / 6,...,69 / 7,...,70 and point at coverage, numCs, numTs; validObject passes. For all 16 rows the reorganized object holds, by content, the counts of exactly the libraries named in sample.ids (harness_capture.R, verify_capture.R).

Coding of every analysis (check 2) against group lists typed by hand from the sheet: indicator 1 and 0 libraries, dropped libraries, covariate columns and values, overdispersion and test all as specified. A3 drops exactly zr3534_4, zr3534_5, zr3534_9, zr3534_10 (18 libraries; ploidy 9 against 9, heat 6 against 12). A4: 12 controls (6 against 6) and 10 heat libraries (5 against 5), no covariate. A5: 11 diploids and 11 triploids (5 heat against 6 control each). A2: 5 triploid heat libraries against 17, covariates ploidy and heat. Residual df 19, 18, 15, 10, 8, 9 as in analyses.csv.

A0 on the subset (check 3): cached A0 fits of the builder's run and of my own from-scratch run, aligned with diffmeth_<contrast>_<mode>.csv.gz by chr and start (not by row): largest relative difference in p 5.12e-15, 5.07e-15, 5.09e-15, 4.97e-15; largest difference in meth.diff 5.33e-14 points; united_row equals the row of the same position in the united table.

A0 on the full data, read-only from the cache of the full run that the parent session started at 04:30:59 (I ran no full fit): A0_ploidy legacy p within 5.3e-15, q within 5.1e-15, 1,038 DML identical with directions; A0_heat legacy p within 5.1e-15, q within 5.0e-15, 2,351 DML identical with directions (the CpG at exactly 20 points, NW_022994958.1:20934, is excluded in both). A2 is the interaction test (check 4): with overdispersion 'none' logReg sets phi = 1, so `test = ifelse(test == "F" & phi > 1, "F", "Chisq")` gives the chi-squared distribution with 1 df. My own glm(cbind(numCs, numTs) ~ ploidy * heat, binomial) against ~ ploidy + heat, p from pchisq(deviance difference, 1): largest relative difference 5.1e-9 at 496 CpGs through the script's fit path, and 5.4e-9 (legacy) and 2.6e-9 (corrected) at about 180 random CpGs of the cached 20,000-row fits. The MN, F version equals my pf(deviance/phi, 1, 18) within 9.7e-9. The script's own coding check has a wide margin: over all 2,896 and 2,806 eligible CpGs of the sample the largest difference is 3.2e-11 and 8.8e-11 against a tolerance of 1e-6 (coding_check_margin.R).

Interaction contrast (check 4): recomputed by hand from group sums for three CpGs (largest, smallest, and closest to the cutoff), for example NC_047568.1:40195657: (66.6667 - 38.7387) - (37.9310 - 80.1653) = 70.1622, file 70.162183, 'hyper'. All 754 and 727 rows of dml_A2_interaction_<mode>.csv, with the four group percentages, equal my recomputation; direction is the sign of (triploid heat - triploid control) - (diploid heat - diploid control). methylKit's meth.diff for this coding equals triploid heat minus all other libraries (hand_interaction.R, verify_outputs.R).

Overdispersion options (check 5): the header's description matches methylKit 1.28.0 logReg line by line (Pearson statistic over length(w) - nprm, values below 1 set to 1, pchisq(deviance/phi, 1) or pf(deviance/phi, 1, residual df) only where phi > 1), the help page and the vignette. My formula-interface GLMs reproduce MN with F and MN with Chisq within 4e-12 for the main effects, and MN with F equals the textbook quasi-binomial F test (anova of quasibinomial fits) within 1.8e-4 where phi > 1, the remainder being the difference between summary.glm's dispersion and the Pearson statistic at the final fit. Full-run caches of A1_ploidy_mn_f and A1_heat_mn_f agree with my GLMs at 400 random rows of the full table (4.0e-9 and 1.0e-11).

Citations (check 5): Akalin et al. 2012 checked in the Europe PMC full text (PMC3491415): the word overdispersion does not occur; the sentence on sample sizes is there; SLIM and the defaults q < 0.01 and 25 percent are as cited. Wang, Tuominen and Tsai 2011, Bioinformatics 27(2):225-231, doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btq650 confirmed. Wreczycka et al. 2017, J Biotechnol 261:105-115, doi:10.1016/j.jbiotec.2017.08.007, PMID 28822795, and the preprint (PPR22834, version of 2017-08-09) confirmed as records only: bioRxiv answered 429 five times, CORE and ScienceDirect 403, so I could not read the quoted sentences. McCullagh and Nelder 1989 is the source the methylKit help page and vignette name. The anova.glm help text is quoted correctly.

DML rule, lists, overlaps, cross-tabulation (check 6): strict inequalities on both criteria (lines 570-571), the same as step 05 line 122 and getMethylDiff. An independent script rebuilt every output of a test run from the cached fits and the step 05 files, matching primary lists by chr and start: all 22 dml_<id>_<mode>.csv files, all columns of dml_counts.csv, both interaction_vs_shared tables, equivalence_with_step05.csv and analyses.csv. 163 comparisons, 0 differences, for the builder's outputs and for my own run; 3,727 spot comparisons of cached p-values with independent GLMs, largest relative difference 9.7e-9 (verify_outputs.R).

Test mode and determinism (checks 8 and 10): the unmodified script (md5 851bdf0c...) run from scratch in a scratch mirror (exit 0, 10.3 min, 2 cores, parent process about 1.3 GB), again from the cache with 1 core (exit 0, 0.2 min, 22 cached fits), and once in the repository from the builder's cache (exit 0): 28 CSVs and the marker file are byte-identical across the builder's run and my three. A file audit (find -newer) shows that a test run writes only under dml_sensitivity/test_subset/; nothing in the full-run folder or in 04_output changed. The full run and the test runs use different cache folders, and the signature holds cpg_set ('all' against 'random subset of 20000, seed 20261119') and n_cpg.

Cache guard (check 9): the signature holds analysis id, mode, md5 of the united file, CpG set, n, methylKit version, library ids, indicator, covariates and their values, overdispersion and test. Altered united_md5: refit, outputs identical. Full-run cache file in the test folder: refit, outputs identical. File cut short: the run stops (finding 2).

Warning policy: count_warnings() counts the four expected messages and turns any other warning into an error; an unexpected warning or an error inside a forked worker reaches the parent as an mclapply warning and stops the run. With more than one core the expected warnings are not collected, as the header says (exp_envvar.R).

Rules (check 10): header has Purpose, Run, Reads, Writes, Notes; helpers used (load_packages, read_libraries, output_path, log_msg, write_table, theme_wgbs, save_figure, mean_percent_methylation, dml_eligible); config$dml_qvalue, dml_difference, cores, modes and colours read from run_config.R; no setwd, no absolute path, no non-ASCII character, no em dash, no 'desiccation', a seed before each of the three random draws, longest line 168 characters. I found no data.table call in which a variable shares a name with a column.

From the full run's caches, dml_counts.csv legacy should show n_dml 2 for A1_ploidy_mn_f and 16 for A1_heat_mn_f (full_dispersion_crosscheck.R, full_pdist.R).
result.notes:
Verdict. I found no error in what the script computes. Object construction, library order, coding of all 16 analyses, the A0 equivalence (subset, and full data for legacy), the interaction test and contrast, the overdispersion options, the DML rule, every output table and the dispersion estimate were reproduced by independent code. The findings concern how the results will be read (finding 1, finding 5) and three robustness gaps (findings 2 to 4). None of them invalidates the fits of the full run that is in progress; every fix is post-processing or text, and the cached fits stay valid because the signature does not depend on the script text.

State of the full run (not started by me; log /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/ed665b6a-3457-5aca-a521-7838dbc31cfa/scratchpad/dml_sensitivity_full.log). Started 04:30:59 with WGBS_CORES=3. A0 legacy passed its check at 04:49:17. Fits take 6.9 to 10.0 minutes each for 22 libraries on the shared machine, which is consistent with the header's estimate. I ran only test-mode runs, harness fits of at most 20,000 CpGs, and read-only comparisons of its cache files.

Corrections to the proposed texts.
1. I-06, Akalin quotation: the sentence in the paper ends '...summed over all samples in each group separately.' The proposed text closes the quotation marks before 'separately'; add the word or an ellipsis.
2. I-06, Wreczycka quotations: I could not open the preprint or the article (see independent checks), so they remain checked by the builder only, through a tool that returns short quotations. Keep the builder's request that someone with journal access confirms them.
3. Header line 147 and the same idea in the log: 'A model fit raises a warning for each CpG where a group has no methylated read' is not accurate. On one core A4_ploidy_in_control logged 'warnings: none' for 20,000 CpGs although 27 percent of them have no methylated read among the controls (p exactly 1); glm.fit converges on the deviance before a fitted value reaches the limit that triggers the warning. Write 'for some CpGs', and do not use the count as a count of such CpGs.
4. I-01: 'share_of_primary_recovered [is] the share of the draft's ploidy DML that one cohort alone supports' is too strong for the uncorrected rows. The cohort's libraries are part of the primary analysis, and the uncorrected within-cohort test treats reads as independent. 'are also called in one cohort alone' is safer.
5. Suggested additions when the full run is in: the reading notes of finding 1; and a note that a list with nearly all loci in one direction (the n_hyper and n_hypo columns) points to a shift of one whole group and not to locus-specific differences. In the test sample the uncorrected interaction and within-cohort lists were strongly one-sided (for example 674 hypo against 80 hyper), which is the pattern of the percent mCpG interaction in Figure 1B. These sample numbers are not results.

Smaller points, not listed as findings. (a) The check that N does not exceed the table size is made per mode (line 520), so a value between 454,555 and 480,579 would run all of legacy mode before corrected mode stops; test both tables before the first fit. (b) step05_file() calls output_path(), which creates 04_output/05_differential_methylation/tables/ if step 05 was never run, before the 'Missing' message; harmless. (c) The DML list files carry no run_scope column; only the folder and the marker file identify a test list.

Substantive result that the parent should carry into I-06 and I-07, after reproducing it in the pipeline: in the draft's analysis the q-value criterion is not binding (finding 1, evidence 1), and the number of ploidy DML (1,038; 952 with the coverage filter) lies inside the range that random relabelling of the animals within each cohort produces (median 736, 13 percent of relabellings give more).
